about: A second set of contributor personas, written and graded by a later reviewer who never saw the ranking code or the first set. Never used for tuning. See evals/README.md.

personas.about: First-year student who has shipped two small iPhone apps in SwiftUI and wants a first open source project, ideally an app that helps people learn.
personas.judge_notes: Only a few orgs ship native iOS code in Swift (Catrobat's Pocket Code for iOS, App Inventor's iOS companion, OneBusAway iOS, Kiwix for Apple). Web-based education orgs match the word 'education' but use none of this person's skills.

personas.about: Backend developer at a small startup who writes Elixir and Phoenix on PostgreSQL and wants to work on realtime chat or messaging software.
personas.judge_notes: No 2026 org uses Elixir, so nothing earns a 3. The tool should fall back to the chat and web backend domain (Zulip, Rocket.Chat, Django) rather than to orgs that just list postgresql or the word real-time.

personas.about: Data engineer with several years of Scala and Spark at work who wants a demanding summer project in functional programming or big data tooling.
personas.judge_notes: Typelevel is the clear match (Scala plus functional programming). Apache lists big data and Java but has 0 projects in 2026, and Java-only orgs like Jenkins or checkstyle match the JVM word without matching either interest.

personas.about: High school student who learned Lua by writing game mods and scripts, has never opened a pull request, and only has a few hours each week.
wrong_top5: Gambit: The package for computation in game theory
personas.judge_notes: The misspelled 'moding' should still reach game tools (Tiled, ScummVM), and Lua should reach Neovim and LabLua. OpenWISP lists lua for router scripts and Gambit matches 'game' only through game theory.

personas.about: Physics PhD student who did all research code in MATLAB and is moving to Python, looking for a scientific project on signal processing or physics simulation.
wrong_top5: Free and Open Source Silicon Foundation
personas.judge_notes: Octave rewards MATLAB skills directly and GNU Radio, gprMax, and TARDIS hit signal processing or physics simulation in Python. Alaska lists matlab but works on radiology and neuroscience, and 'simulation' alone pulls in network, circuit, and robot simulators.

personas.about: Web developer who writes internal CLI tools and build scripts in TypeScript and Node and wants to work on tools other programmers use every day.
personas.judge_notes: webpack and Gemini CLI match all three interests in TypeScript and Node. Compiler and static analysis orgs are tagged 'development tools' but need C++, Java, Kotlin, or Haskell, and TypeScript alone pulls in unrelated apps.

personas.about: Bootcamp graduate who writes C# with .NET and has made small Unity games, looking for a first open source project around games or desktop apps.
wrong_top5: Gambit: The package for computation in game theory
personas.judge_notes: No org is built on C# and only JSON Schema mentions .NET, for a validator library far from games. Best bets are a Java desktop app (JabRef, an easy move from C#) and Tiled, a game level editor many Unity developers already use.

personas.about: Firmware engineer who writes embedded Rust and C for microcontrollers at work and wants a full-time summer project on space or robotics systems.
personas.judge_notes: RTEMS (an RTOS used in spacecraft), LibreCube (space hardware with Rust), dora-rs (Rust robotics), and ArduPilot (vehicle firmware) fit an embedded engineer. Many orgs list rust for desktop or media apps, and astronomy orgs match 'space' through data analysis, not hardware.

personas.about: Linguistics major who taught herself Python and NLTK to study text corpora; she types quickly and misspells her interests.
personas.judge_notes: Fuzzy matching must recover 'linguistics' (CDLI) and 'natural language processing' (Accord Project, HumanAI). 'Procesing' must not drift to the Processing Foundation, and 'language' must not drift to programming language orgs.

personas.about: Journalism student who makes interactive charts and maps with D3 and Leaflet for class projects and has never contributed to open source.
wrong_top5: Gambit: The package for computation in game theory
personas.judge_notes: The profile names only JavaScript libraries, never the language, so the tool has to infer JavaScript web mapping. Many Python science orgs carry a 'visualization' tag but would not use D3 or Leaflet skills.

personas.about: Junior backend developer who builds Spring Boot services on PostgreSQL and wants a summer project where the code helps clinics and hospitals.
personas.judge_notes: OpenELIS Global (Java, Spring, PostgreSQL) and OpenMRS (Java medical records) fit both skills and domain. Java-only dev tools and orgs that just list postgresql for unrelated work should stay out of the top five.

personas.about: Technical writer who writes clear Markdown guides and uses Git but codes very little, and can give about four hours a week.
personas.judge_notes: GSoC is a coding program, so nothing is a strong fit. The best options are orgs with docs, website, or learning-material projects that need light code. Orgs that only list git as a tool, or that match 'document' or 'writing', are traps, and the tool should warn that 4 hours a week is below what even a small project needs.
